The first two tiers – the companies most directly exposed to a Chevron outage – are listed below. | | 2️⃣ | **Corpus searches** for any filing that mentions the disruption and the downstream firms identified in step 1 | • A search for *“Chevron refinery outage August 2012 … Indian Oil / Toyota”* returned only generic Chevron filings (refinery projects, sales volumes) and a set of Toyota‑Motor annual‑report excerpts that discuss unrelated cost‑reduction and recall matters.
• A second search for *“Chevron Indian Oil 2012”* produced a Chevron filing that mentions its historic 5 % stake in Reliance’s Jamnagar refinery (sold in 2009) – again, no reference to an August 2012 disruption or any impact on Indian Oil.
• No other downstream company name appeared in the returned documents. | | 3️⃣ | **Cross‑checking** (attempted second source per firm) | Because the corpus searches yielded only the above generic Chevron filings, there was no second independent source (e.g., a supplier’s own filing) that could confirm an actual operational impact on any downstream customer or partner. No filing or news item (within the four tool calls) mentions any impact from the August 2012 event. | | **Toyota Motor** | Appears in the graph (Tier 1). A corpus search returned Toyota’s 2012 annual‑report excerpts, but those discuss cost‑reduction, recalls and unrelated supply‑chain issues – **no mention of a Chevron outage or any effect on Toyota’s production**. | | **Cummins** | Listed as downstream; no specific filing or news item retrieved that connects the August 2012 Chevron event to Cummins’ engine business. | | **Lanxess**, **SK**, **E1**, **Jordan Petroleum Refinery**, **Volkswagen**, **BP**, **BHP**, **Mahindra & Mahindra**, **Tata Motors**, **Stellantis**, etc. | All appear in the graph, but none were found in any of the returned corpus documents or Chevron filings that discuss an August 2012 disruption. Consequently there is **no corroborating evidence** (from the limited tool budget) that they experienced a material impact. | *Because only four tool calls were permitted, we could not request each company’s own 10‑K/20‑F filing (via `get_supplier_info`) to look for “Chevron” or “refinery outage” mentions. The corpus searches exhausted the remaining two calls and returned no relevant disclosures.* --- ## What **could NOT** be confirmed | Item | Reason it remains unverified | |------|------------------------------| | **Actual operational impact on any downstream company** (e.g., reduced fuel deliveries, production slow‑downs) | No filing, press release or SEC disclosure within the searched corpus mentions the August 2012 Chevron event for any of the listed firms. | | **Quantitative loss estimates** (volume shortfalls, revenue hit) for downstream customers | Same as above – no evidence was retrieved. | | **Alternative suppliers stepping in** (e.g., other refiners filling the gap) | The traversal shows possible alternative‑supplier nodes, but none were identified in the limited filings as having taken over Chevron’s volumes during that period. | | **Specific supplier‑level disruptions for Tier 2 firms** (e.g., Toyota‑Boshoku, Volkswagen) | No direct references found; only structural connections are known from the graph. | --- ## Bottom line - The **structural supply‑chain map** shows a large set of downstream entities—spanning oil & gas producers, chemicals, automotive manufacturers and component makers—that would be exposed to a prolonged Chevron refinery outage. - Within the four allowed tool calls we were only able to retrieve **generic Chevron operational disclosures** (refinery projects, sales volumes) and **unrelated Toyota annual‑report excerpts**. None of these documents mention the August 2012 disruption nor any downstream impact on the listed firms. - Consequently, while the *potential* at‑risk list is well defined by the graph, **no concrete evidence was found to confirm that any specific downstream company actually suffered a material effect** from the reported Chevron event. > **Result:** The investigation identifies many companies that could be affected in theory, but due to tool‑call limits and lack of explicit disclosures, the actual impact on each downstream firm remains **unverified**. Further research (e.g., direct 10‑K/20‑F look‑ups for each company) would be required to move from “structurally at risk” to “confirmed impacted”.
